Subject: Private VPC deployment — plane segmentation, cutover scenarios & ops checklist

Alex / Stella infra team — thanks again for the prep call yesterday. I pulled together a short set of operational scenarios for the upcoming pilot cutover so we can align control-plane/data-plane boundaries, egress fallback behavior, and the runbook steps for the first customer environment. See attached: vpc-segmentation-v1.pdf and ops-cutover-checklist.md.

High-level asks for this thread:
- Confirm the control-plane endpoints that must remain on the management VPC vs what can be proxied through customer egress.
- Approve the fallback sequence if the primary egress is blocked (we propose a queued local-kv cache + outbound relay via EdgeCloud).
- Identify any on-prem firewall rules or NAT mappings you need from the customer's side for the handoff window.

Notes and open questions in the PDF (page 3): certificate exchange timing during cutover, and whether Customer A requires HSM-backed key wraps (if so, we'll need the KMS stub configured before the window).

Proposed calendar: pilot cutover Saturday (2026-12-12) morning, dry-run Thursday (2026-12-10) in staging. Can everyone confirm availability?

Thanks,

Vanessa — thanks for the packet, looks clear and thoughtful. Quick answers inline: 

- Control plane endpoints: EdgeCloud can host the management proxies for model pulling and metrics aggregation. We'll keep the control-plane TLS termination inside customer VPC for keys (option A on page 2). That means we need the KMS integration by dry-run.

- Egress fallback: The queued local-KV idea fits well. One ask: if primary egress fails, can Redwood's runtime fallback to a relay authenticated via mTLS to our relay cluster? That avoids long-lived creds on customer nodes.

- Firewall/NAT: Customer A needs two outbound ports open: 443 (mTLS) and 5222 (for our lightweight control heartbeat). We'll send a one-page firewall table to procurement.

We can make staging dry-run on 12/10 at 09:00 PT. Saturday cutover looks good for us as well.

I'll upload a short Relay runbook tonight to the shared Drive.

—Alex
Alex Ramos | Director, Integrations — EdgeCloud Solutions

Thanks Alex / Vanessa — a couple operational clarifications after reviewing the PDF and relay notes: 

1) Certificate exchange window: we need the customer to apply their CA bundle to the control-plane proxy at least 48 hours prior to the dry-run. Otherwise cert pinning will fail during handshake. (Page 3 highlights this.)

2) Fallback auth: mTLS relay is our preference (Alex's suggestion). We'll require a short-lived cert issued by Redwood's control-plane CA and rotated during handoff. Ops will automate this via the ops-cutover-checklist.md step 5.

3) KV cache eviction policy: for the queued local-KV, recommend LRU with max_age 12h and a separate backpressure metric so we can abort heavy workloads during degraded egress. Add metric name: runtime.kv.local_backpressure.

Action items for this thread: 
- Alex: send the Relay runbook + firewall table by EOD Mon.
- Vanessa: confirm whether Customer A requires HSM for key-wrap (yes/no) so Irene can scope the KMS prep.
- Karthik: can you review the ops-cutover-checklist.md and add the exact CLI commands for cert rotation?

On availability: I can attend dry-run 12/10 09:00 PT and cutover 12/12 morning.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Product Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick follow-up after reading the checklist and the segmentation PDF. I made three small edits in ops-cutover-checklist.md (attached as inline notes in the Drive link): 

- Added explicit cert rotation CLI (openssl + our cert-rotate helper) and an automated verification step that hits /healthz on the control-plane proxy.
- Clarified the order: (1) customer CA applied; (2) control-plane short-lived cert issued; (3) control-plane cert deployed; (4) sanity checks; (5) start routing. This ordering avoids a momentary split-brain where the runtime accepts but management rejects.
- Added an abort threshold: if runtime.kv.local_backpressure > 0.8 for 5 minutes, trigger rollback to staged config and open incident.

I'm good for the dry-run and Saturday cutover. One last ask: Alex / EdgeCloud — can you confirm whether your relay supports SNI passthrough for multi-tenant hostnames or if we'll need per-tenant mTLS endpoints? If per-tenant endpoints are required, we'll add that to the ops checklist and change the firewall table.

Thanks all,
